Tree reconstruction
dump.txt (commit aedb777, 2026-08-12) split and SHA-256 verified: 334 of 334 files match. The only mismatch is export.sh itself, which is expected — the dump embeds a nested copy of the script that writes it, producing a phantom # FILE: ${SCRIPT_NAME} header.

Incidental corroboration: the eleven files that needed extra trailing-newline handling to hash correctly are exactly the eleven Slice 35 recorded as ending in two or more LFs — .env.example, ci.yml, backup.sh, restore_drill.sh, SignIn.razor, CounterBoard.razor, AccountEndpoints.cs, IdentityServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, ObligationsEnforcement.cs, CounterJourneys.cs, IdentityWiringTests.cs. That open item is real and reproducible from the dump alone.

What is actually red
Slice 35 did not fail a test. MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests does not compile, so it never ran. Three sites, one mistake:

tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Components/HandheldLayoutContractTests.cs
  1113,48  CS1503: cannot convert from 'System.StringComparison' to 'int'
  1115,52  same
  1121,53  same
All three are in DeclarationBlocksIn — css.IndexOf('{', open + 1, StringComparison.Ordinal).

I verified the overload set against dotnet/runtime@release/10.0 rather than asserting it from memory. String.Searching.cs declares, for char: IndexOf(char), IndexOf(char, int), IndexOf(char, StringComparison), IndexOf(char, int, int). There is no (char, int, StringComparison) — argument 3 binds to count. For string the same overload does exist, which is what makes the trap asymmetric and worth a ledger row. Also confirmed: LastIndexOf(char, StringComparison) doesn't exist at all, and IndexOf(char, StringComparison.Ordinal) delegates literally to IndexOf(char) — so dropping the third argument at all three sites, and the redundant second at line 1111, is behaviour-identical. The repo's own convention already omits it (text.IndexOf('>', index), body.IndexOf('"', open + 1)).

Everything else was green: Domain, DataAccess, E2E 16/16, boot smoke, compose-substitution gate, tree hygiene, governance, shellcheck. 497 tests ran; the web-layer project's ~580 didn't.

The two new facts do pass
I ported all nine HandheldLayoutContractTests facts plus TestingSectionContractTests to Python (35 assertions) and ran them against the verified tree: 10 facts, 0 failing assertions. The compile error is the only thing between this tree and green.

Proven sensitive, and specifically on the helper being repaired: a colour planted inside app.css's breakpoint query is reported — which is what shows the nested at-rule descent works. Proven not to fire: #abcdef-notice and 
#fedcba as id-selector preludes, and background-color: transparent. (#blazor-error-ui is already in the real stylesheet at line 840, so that case is exercised by the tree itself.)

The register stopped being a table
This is the larger finding, and it's the one your notes flagged. TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md Appendix A:

Header declares three columns; every row from F-38 to F-70 carries four (F-41 carries five). Markdown truncates to the header's count, so the Embodied in cell — the file paths and the BUILD_PROGRESS slice, the entire "→ embodiment" half of "ruling → embodiment" — is silently dropped on roughly thirty rows. The heading sits above the Decision text instead.
F-63 through F-70 are outside the table entirely. Line 1259 is a --- horizontal rule; the eight rows after it have no header and no delimiter, so all of Slices 33–35 render as literal pipe-delimited text.
F-65 has no row. It's concatenated onto the end of F-64's line by a stray || at column 3089.
Two blank lines before ## Changelog.
DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md has the same class of damage in Group E: F-38's row carries five cells against a four-column header, and blank lines at 79–81, 83, 85, 87, 89, 91, 93, 95, 97, 99, 107, 109 and 117 break one table into fourteen fragments — every fragment after the first losing its header, so the ID column stops being a column.

The tiebreaker for the repair is that DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md's four tables all use | ID | Finding | Ruling | Embodied in |. The newer Appendix A rows are following the ledger's shape correctly; the header is the stale part. So Appendix A goes to four columns, and the ~17 older compressed rows (| F-20 | Hand-written fakes… | §16.1 |) get an em-dash in the narrative column rather than invented history.

F-72 — the register that isn't a table. Both documents repaired, and this one does name something executable: DefectRegisterContractTests.cs, asserting that every pipe-delimited row in docs/ sits under a delimiter row and carries exactly its header's column count, with a non-vacuity floor.

Files to DELETE: none. One git add required — the new test file. No new directory. Seven full files, repo-relative, extractable in one operation at the repo root; I verified the round trip by extracting over a fresh copy of your tree and confirming the result is byte-identical to the tree I ran everything against.

Read this first
Slice 35 did not fail a test. It never ran one. dotnet test printed total: 497, failed: 0 and then Build failed with 3 error(s) — the 497 are Domain, DataAccess and all sixteen scenarios, all passing, while MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests never compiled and its ~580 assertions never executed, including both facts that slice existed to add.

Three findings
F-71 — an overload that exists for string and not for char. DeclarationBlocksIn called IndexOf('{', open + 1, StringComparison.Ordinal) three times. I read the overload set from dotnet/runtime@release/10.0 rather than recalling it: for char there is IndexOf(char), (char, int), (char, StringComparison), (char, int, int) — and no three-argument-with-comparison form, though string has one. Argument three binds to count, so CS1503 reports a type mismatch on an argument instead of a missing member. The fix drops the argument and is behaviour-identical: in that same file IndexOf(char, StringComparison.Ordinal) returns IndexOf(value), and IndexOf(char, int) returns IndexOf(value, startIndex, Length - startIndex).

F-72 — both registers had stopped being tables. Found by opening Appendix A to add F-71's row and discovering I couldn't, because there was no answer to how many columns a row has. Appendix A's header declared three columns while every row from F-38 onward carried four, so the Embodied in cell was being discarded on thirty rows of the register whose whole subject is ruling → embodiment. F-63 to F-70 sat outside the table behind a horizontal rule. F-65 had no row at all, fused onto F-64's by a stray pipe pair. And in the ledger, thirty-one rows were broken into fourteen fragments. Nothing was ever wrong in the source — it was wrong only once rendered, and it accumulated in the one direction nothing could catch, because each slice appended a row shaped like the last one.

F-73 — the gate against stale counts shipped with a stale count. TestingSectionContractTests said §16.4 "carries eight of them" when it carried nine, while its own floor said nine. Both move to ten.

Two things worth your attention
No gate was added for F-71, and that's a ruling. The compiler is the gate; it ran and it blocked. A test re-asserting what CSC rejects is the monument F-47 says to delete. What failed was my pre-delivery verification, so §18 gained the habit instead: build the archive before believing its verification notes.

The new gate found two false positives in itself before I shipped it, both in your tree rather than planted. OPERATIONS.md correctly escapes a shell pipeline inside a table cell, and BUILD_PROGRESS.md quotes eighteen fenced log lines that each open with a pipe. The first draft reported both on correct documents — F-41 exactly. It then caught my own two new ledger rows, seven cells wide, for the same unescaped-pipe reason.

Verification: 334/334 files SHA-verified from the dump; ten ported facts with thirty-five assertions passing; the new gate at 41 findings before and 0 after; ten of ten §16.4 counts agreeing; bracket, CS1620, CS4007 and overload scans clean and each proven sensitive. Nothing compiled — MarkdownTableContractTests is the only new C# file and uses two nested sealed record declarations, which nothing else in that project does.

Predicted test count 1082 (1078 last observed, +2 for Slice 35's facts now able to run, +2 for this slice's). Arithmetic, not an observation — if the run says otherwise, that difference is the next thing to chase.

One thing I found and deliberately left: F-41 is cited fifteen times in DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md and has no row of its own there. Whether to write the row or accept that Appendix A is the register of record for gate-scope rulings is a decision, not a repair, and it's recorded in Still open rather than made inside a slice about table structure.
